item.title: How Warriors energizer Charles ‘Basketball' Bassey is trying to seize center opportunity
item.description: Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey shoots against Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks during the second half Monday in San Francisco. (Jed Jacobsohn/AP) The exercise bike spun, aimlessly, for an entire fourth quarter in Phoenix. Charles Bassey hardly hopped off, a young man who'd spent much of the previous few days with ice packs wrapped around his knees. He certainly didn't hop off to hop back on the court, and his season debut was hard-capped at a mild 13 minutes in an Oct. 24 loss to the Suns. Bassey understood. He had knee tendinitis. He was also frustrated. He spent most of his five previous NBA seasons watching from the sidelines, ailments wracking an otherwise-twitchy 6-foot-10 frame. He is tired of watching. So that night, he went to Drew Yoder, Golden State's director of medical services, and questioned why he didn't play the fourth quarter of an all-hands-on-deck game. Two days later, he lounged with ice packs on knees at a Warriors shootaround. A horse, raring. "I think I'm an asset to the team," Bassey told the Chronicle. "And they know that, too. I just gotta keep bringing that every game. And understand, every time, that every game is going to be a ramp-up. "And when I'm there," he continued, "you guys are gonna know. You guys are gonna know, bro." There was Monday night, when the Warriors needed him most. After a spot-start Sunday night against the Clippers, Bassey was, again, watching from the bench when Draymond Green tossed Suns big Khaman Maluach to the hardwood and then went face-to-face with Dillon Brooks. Green exited, ejected. Bassey entered, energized. Options were few. The only other available center was two-way rookie Graham Ike. Al Horford was resting, which will be a common occurrence for the 40-year-old this year. Kristaps Porzingis is, well, somewhere; in the latest chapter of an utterly bizarre saga , head coach Steve Kerr said pregame he has not communicated with Porzingis and does not know where he is. The tenor of Monday's 116-113 win, though - five straight - shifted with Bassey, the man who's been waiting for this. "Those are the patterns of what a good team does, when, night after night, you're finding combinations - you're finding production up and down the bench, and you love it," Stephen Curry said postgame. "Like, everybody feeds off that energy, when a guy comes in like that, like Bass did tonight, changes the game. Everybody notices. Lifts everybody's spirits." Exactly 19 seconds of clock into arriving on the floor, Bassey finished a tip-plus-foul off a missed Yaxel Lendeborg three. He swarmed the glass. He maintained paint presence against a Suns team that went small. He established a burgeoning connection with 24-year-old rookie Lendeborg, who found him for a third-quarter lob. And he got into a skirmish of his own, sneering at Suns forward Miles Bridges after Bridges shoved him following a jump-ball tie-up with Phoenix guard Jalen Green. item.title: 🎥 Man Utd fans launch protests inside Old Trafford amid UCL clash
item.description: 🎥 Man Utd fans launch protests inside Old Trafford amid UCL clash Manchester United's miserable season is continuing to plunge fresh depths. Already in the grip of relegation form in the Premier League, Michael Carrick's side are also out of luck in Europe after shipping two quick-fire goals at home to Roma. Even before the visitors raced into their early lead, the Old Trafford faithful were clear on the source of their ongoing problems and took aim at those in the boardroom. Before kick-off, Red Devils fans released hundreds of green and gold balloons in a nod to their previous protests against the club's majority owners, the Glazer family. If that made uncomfortable viewing for the American overlords, worse was still to follow when the game ticked into 20:05, symbolising the year that they took charge. Tennis balls were launched onto the pitch from the Stretford End and beyond, forcing United's latest Champions League encounter to be brought to a temporary halt. Chants against the Glazers were also routinely aired including ones imploring them to 'sell up' after 21 years of financial mismanagement and chaotic decision-making.

item.title: Connecticut brothers pull 1-in-10.5-million Tom Brady card from $30 box
item.description: Lucas Martell (left) and Trevor Martell pose with the Tom Brady card outside of The Treasure Chest of Mystic. (Courtesy of David Tranchida) It's no secret that the sports and trading card market has exploded in recent years . Just this year, a 2026 Topps Chrome Ohtani Dual Gold Logoman card sold for $11 million while a 2025-26 Topps Chrome Update NBA Debut Patch Auto from Cooper Flagg fetched just over $8 million. Though not every card that is pulled from a pack of Topps will command a seven- or eight-figure sale, there are occasionally special cards found within these packs that turn $30 into a game-changing investment. One of these special cards was pulled last month by two Jewett City brothers, effectively altering their lives. Lucas, 23, and Trevor Martell, 18, purchased three $30 boxes of Topps NFL Bowman sports cards from Target on October 15, with each brother taking one box for themselves while making a deal to open the third box in the car. Inside that box was a one-of-one "Bejeweled Brady" Garbage Pail Kids Superfractor card. Featuring a gold border and lettering, Lucas Martell knew something special was in the pack that he was opening before he saw what it was. "We kind of like lost it right then and there," Lucas Martell said. "I knew it was a special card, but I didn't realize how special it was until afterwards." The "Bejeweled Brady" Garbage Pail Kids Superfractor is a one-of-one card depicting the famed NFL player. (Courtesy of David Tranchida) The odds of pulling the card? Mathematical estimates put it at one in 10.5 million. And the best part? It wasn't the only expensive card in the pack. "Right behind that card, there was a Drake Maye, it's called the Etched in Glass, and that card's worth like $200 itself," Lucas Martell said. What makes the card so special is the collaboration between Garbage Pail Kids and Topps. Since the card is the only one of its kind in existence, the resale value skyrockets. A similar one-of-one Garbage Pail Kids Superfractor of Flagg sold for $288,000 , making it the most expensive Garbage Pail Kids card of all time, according to Topps. Being that the card is of Brady adds more value, as cards of the seven-time Super Bowl champion have climbed as high as $3.1 million . Lucas Martell said he recently got into collecting sports trading cards while his brother has been a longtime fan of cards. Part of getting into collecting typically involves visiting hobby shops, which the brothers did with the newly opened Treasure Chest of Mystic in Olde Mistick Village . The brothers quickly befriended shop owner Carmine Lorusso, who helped them through the process of bringing it to an upcoming auction from Fanatics. (L-R) Michael Carini, Lucas Martell, Trevor Martell and Carmine Lorusso pose with the Tom Brady card outside of The Treasure Chest of Mystic. item.title: Rafa Camara to debut in F1 Brazil GP as Esteban Ocon out at Haas
item.description: Motorsport photo The Haas F1 team has decided Esteban Ocon will not race again for the squad, with 2027 debutant Rafa Camara getting an early debut this weekend on home soil. Following increasingly strained relations between Ocon and the team, a heated argument in Mexico proved the final straw that made team principal Ayao Komatsu decide to bench the Frenchman. Ferrari junior Camara, who had already been signed by Haas to replace Ocon for 2027, will take the wheel of the WF-26 at Interlagos and will remain in the car for Las Vegas. Toyota protege Ryo Hirakawa, who scored a point on his debut last weekend in Mexico, will finish the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, provided those races take place as planned. "We have now notified Esteban Ocon that he will not return to a race seat with TGR Haas F1 Team this season," Komatsu explained. "Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward. The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations." More to follow. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. item.title: The biggest controversies of Carson Hocevar's chaotic 2026 NASCAR Cup season
item.description: Motorsport photo Carson 'Hurricane' Hocevar has been the story of the 2026 season, making headlines almost every week. Some of those moments were positive, like his epic Talladega win and post-race celebration, or his fan outreach and incredible merchandise sales. He made the Time 100 list for 'Most Influential People in Sports' and even attended the Met Gala. However, there's been plenty of negativity as well, and he will now end the NASCAR Cup season on the sidelines due to his most recent actions at Martinsville, with Spire Motorsports suspending him. Veteran drivers have been loudly critical of him throughout the year, even questioning if he cares more about fame than racing results at times. So, we decided to recap just some of the biggest controversies that defined Hocevar's wild year behind the wheel of the No. 77 Chevrolet: Punching Ryan Blaney at Bristol RYAN BLANEY AND CARSON HOCEVAR FIGHT AT BRISTOL!!! https://t.co/da4ls6i24P — Motorsport (@Motorsport) September 20, 2026 This moment will likely be remembered more than any other in the long-run. Hocevar was in contention for the win at Bristol, but while battling Ryan Blaney for second, Hocevar sent him crashing into the wall after a failed block by the Penske driver, while he went on to finish third. After the race, Blaney approached him on pit road and grabbed Hocevar, who immediately starting throwing haymakers. Hocevar punched Blaney twice in the scuffle. Hocevar told a later press scrum that he had never hit anyone before Saturday night, and thinks NASCAR would "lose ticket sales" if they dished out fines for the altercation. As for Blaney, he ended up regretting his part in the fight, and no penalties were issued. item.description: The Favre Sides (Nov. 18, 1996) originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . God, how Brett Favre hates to be boring. Things dull in the locker room? How about a little heat-generating ointment in somebody's underwear? Party a drag? How about a drop-dead imitation of sportscaster Keith “Whoa Nellie” Jackson? Golf game not lively enough? How about a 3-wood between trees, over water, aimed at a target Tiger Woods couldn't reach? Brash Brett is high energy bottled up in a swashbuckler's frame, thriving on the rush generated by his ability to produce the unexpected. He is a living remote control, channel surfing through life, searching constantly for snippets of action, his attention span tested by even a 30-second television commercial. But over the past few seasons, despite his natural resistance, another Favre has gradually developed. Boring Brett. He is a bit more practical, slightly more level-headed, a tad more mature than Brash Brett. Boring Brett is the one who has grown to like demanding Packers coach Mike Holmgren and even discovered life isn't necessarily a non-stop frat party, particularly after spending part of the summer shaking an addiction to painkillers. Brash Brett doesn't exactly embrace Boring Brett; something about how being dull contradicts his much-preferred image of a maverick bent on doing just about everything in a slightly different way than society might approve. 'Tell me not to stick my hand in the cookie jar and I may not do it right then, but sooner or later, I'll be in that jar,” Brash Brett says. But like it or not, Boring Brett has taken up permanent residence in the recesses of Favre's mind. Every time Favre drops back to pass, Brash Brett and Boring Brett wrestle for control of the remote that runs that brain. Brash Brett, the gunslinger, looks over the defense and sees a potential touchdown in an area where no sane quarterback would risk throwing. “Fans'll love that one,” he thinks, imagining himself rolling away from pressure, launching the ball, watching it streaking through two straining defenders and landing in the arms of a leaping receiver deep in the end zone. If the reaction isn't—”How did he do that?”—Brash Brett is disappointed. Boring Brett, the common-sense guy, methodically searches for the most logical target, even if it means a ho-hum 2-yard gain to a back who has quietly moved into the flat. “Coach'll love that one,” he thinks. And if fans have to stifle yawns, so what? As much as he hates to admit it, even Brash Brett concedes if he becomes boring enough, the Packers will win a Super Bowl. No question, he has the physical talent to get them there; Boring Brett just needs to funnel it properly and not let Brash Brett attempt too many outlandish plays.
